title: Multiline validation bypass
blurb: Demonstrates how /^[a-z.-]+$/m accepts an injected line in a hostname allowlist, then fixes it with \A...\z alongside per-line ^/$ rules and \Z for single values with one trailing newline.
question: Can \A...\z eliminate multiline allowlist bypasses while preserving per-line ^/$ matching and CRLF/trailing-newline handling via \Z?
result: Verified in Chrome 153 headless: /^[a-z.-]+$/m accepts payloads with an injected invalid line, while \A(?:^...$(?:\r\n|\n)?)+\z/mu rejects injected lines and tolerates trailing newlines and CRLF identically both natively (with V8 flag) and via the labelled modifier-group fallback (flag-off).
testedIn: Chrome for Testing 153.0.8010.12 (default and --js-flags=--js-regexp-buffer-boundaries); not verified flag-free in Chrome 160

friction.summary: Combining the m flag with ^ and $ allows a single valid line to bypass whole-input validation when an attacker injects extra lines
friction.repro: Test a multi-line payload containing one valid hostname line and one injected line against /^[a-z.-]+$/m; test() returns true because ^ and $ match any single line boundary.
friction.workaround: Wrap whole-payload validators in \A...\z (with u or v flag) when m is enabled, or use (?-m:^) and (?-m:$) where buffer boundaries are not yet supported.
